recorded: Every case passed 7 runs against the original with Node.js 26.12.1, @langchain/core 1.1.19, @langchain/langgraph 1.2.0, @langchain/mcp-adapters 1.1.3, @langchain/openai 1.2.5, langchain 1.2.18, fastify 5.7.4, @erickwendel/ew-customers-mcp 0.0.13, @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem 2.0.1, curl 8.7.1, and jq 1.7.1. Each case names its program, and one shell command run from the module chose by it: start ran node src/index.ts without a .env file, the file npm start runs with one, and token ran sh getServiceToken.sh. The original always calls OpenRouter's address, so the copy that produced these cases reads OPENAI_BASE_URL first and falls back to it, a one-line change in the OpenRouter service. No OpenRouter key was available, so the model answers were recorded from Ollama 0.40.11 through its OpenAI-compatible API, with gpt-oss:20b standing in for arcee-ai/trinity-large-preview:free at low reasoning effort, set by a proxy in front of Ollama, and without the stand-in's reasoning field, while the requests keep the model the program asked for. The stand-in created the customers one call at a time. OpenRouter's refusal of an empty key is synthesized from its documented error format, and the client sends Bearer alone, while a key left unset fails in the client before any request, which the cases cannot express. The published customers server and getServiceToken.sh always call http://localhost:9999/v1, so the cases put the replay on port 9999, beside the model's answers, and the entry point always listens on port 3000, so both must be free. The API's answers were recorded from this lesson's API, nodejs-fastify-mongodb-crud-z, on an empty MongoDB, through the same proxy, and the customers' answers require the service token it issued, which SERVICE_TOKEN holds, as a bearer. Both MCP servers start through npx at @latest, so npx needs registry.npmjs.org, and the cases compare none of their results directly: the API's answers must show in the output after each customers call, and the filesystem server writes ./data/users.json inside its allowed data folder, as data/data/users.json, which the cases read. The first write fails while data/data is missing and succeeds once a run has created it, so the tool messages are checked by their call ids alone. Both .env cases leave the folder as it was.
originals: case {program} in start) node src/index.ts ;; token) sh getServiceToken.sh ;; esac

cases.name: the sample question runs the agent once, which creates three customers one at a time through the published customers server with its service token as a bearer, lists them, and writes them through the filesystem server to ./data/users.json, which the server resolves inside its allowed data folder as data/data/users.json, then answers 200 with the model's text
